blocks.title: a lead is *60x* more likely to talk to you if you do one boring thing

blocks.caption: it's from a harvard study, not my opinion, so swipe.

blocks.text:
researchers looked at 1.25 million sales leads from 42 US companies.

firms that answered within an hour were **nearly 7x more likely** to get a real conversation with the decision maker than firms that waited just one more hour.

compared to firms that waited a day or more, it was **more than 60x**.

rows.label: waited 24 hours or more
rows.caption: yes, that's one dot vs sixty, on the same scale.

blocks.text:
it's not a better hook or a fancier funnel. it's replying while they still care.

i know, you were hoping for a secret.

harvard also sent a fake lead to 2,241 companies, just to time the reply.

**23% never answered at all.** the ones who did took 42 hours on average.

blocks.title: posting more won't fix a slow *inbox*

blocks.text: a viral Reel just means **more people waiting** for an answer.

that study was about web forms and emails, back in 2011.

today your leads show up in your DMs at 11:47 pm, straight from a Reel, with the attention span of a goldfish on espresso.

i'd bet the clock runs even faster there.

being fast doesn't mean replying in 0.3 seconds with a link. that's just a faster way to sound like a bot.

what i'd do: answer within the hour, wait until they finish typing, then ask **one question** about them.
